101: Entitlement to a FERS retirement annuity: whether Reid's military service counts toward the five-year civilian service eligibility requirement under 5 U.S.C. 8410 and 8411.
The plain language of § 8410 requires five years of civilian service.
313: Retirement annuity overpayment and waiver of repayment under FERS; whether the annuitant was without fault and recovery would be against equity and good conscience; commencement date of annuity.
We agree with the government that substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that Lua was not without fault for the overpayment.
314: Commencement date of FERS annuity (January 27, 2000 versus September 9, 2001) used to calculate retroactive benefits; OPM's selection of earlier date upheld as not arbitrary.
Accordingly, we agree with the government that the regulations expressly authorize beginning Lua's annuity on January 27, 2000, the day after her pay ceased.
506: Entitlement to a CSRS deferred retirement annuity; whether Hocson served in a position covered by CSRS, so as to meet the creditable and covered service requirements of 5 U.S.C. § 8333 and 5 C.F.R. § 831.112.
We discern no error in the Board's determination that Mr. Hocson had not served in a position covered by the CSRS.
649: Calculation of CSRS high-three average pay for retirement annuity: the Board and OPM relied on an incorrect legal ground that reported retirement deductions are dispositive, and the court found the Form 2806 internally contradictory on overtime pay, so the Board's decision was vacated and remanded for determination of the actual overtime pay.
We vacate the Board's decision and remand for a determination of that issue.
654: Entitlement to a former spouse survivor annuity; MSPB held Emond not entitled because the divorce decree on which OPM's award was based was found inaccurate by a Virginia court, and the court affirmed.
Accordingly, we affirm the MSPB's determination that Ms. Emond is not entitled to a survivor annuity.
664: Entitlement to CSRS annuity: Francisco lacked the required covered service under 5 U.S.C. 8333(b) because his Navy appointments were excepted or indefinite and not subject to CSRS.
The Board and OPM correctly determined that Francisco did not have the necessary covered service to qualify for an annuity under 5 U.S.C. § 8333(b).
665: Right to make a retroactive deposit under 5 C.F.R. 831.303(a) to cure the lack of covered service; denied because a former employee not already covered by CSRS cannot make a deposit.
Because Francisco did not have any covered service during his employment with the Navy, a deposit under 5 C.F.R. § 831.303(a) cannot cure this defect in his application for a CSRS annuity.
678: Entitlement to former spouse survivor annuity: whether OPM could process a 2013 amended domestic relations order that modified the survivor annuity after the employee's 2010 retirement; held barred by 5 U.S.C. 8341(h)(4) and 5 C.F.R. 838.806(b).

The Board correctly concluded that OPM was barred by statute and regulation from processing Alan's change request based on the 2013 amended domestic relations order because that order modified the June 1995 order and, as is undisputed, it issued after Alan had already retired.
692: Entitlement to the lump-sum credit payable to a survivor under 5 U.S.C. § 8342, turning on the decedent's pay status and the amount of deductions refundable; the court affirmed the Board's finding that the decedent was not in pay status after August 18, 1972, so the lump-sum amount OPM calculated stands.
We have no difficulty concluding that the evidence of record fully supports the Board's finding as to when Ms. Nelson was in pay status.
736: Entitlement to FERS disability retirement: the Board's affirmance of OPM's denial of Lamb's application, finding he did not establish a disabling medical condition while employed in a FERS position.
Although we may have reached a different conclusion in this case had we been the fact-finding body, we cannot review denials of disability for substantial evidence.
748: Entitlement to FERS survivor annuity: the court held Becker was not a 'widow' under 5 U.S.C. § 8441(1) because the marriage lasted less than nine months, so OPM's denial of survivor benefits was affirmed.
OPM had denied her benefits because she had been married to Mr. Mayberry for less than nine months
808: Entitlement to disability retirement: whether mental incompetence excused the late filing (substantial evidence he was not incompetent), and whether a presumption of disability applied because disability caused separation (AJ found it did not).
Substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that Stussy was not incompetent.
954: FERS disability annuitant's overpayment waiver: the Board's 'without fault' finding rested on a legally erroneous reading of OPM's Prompt Notification Exception and Set-Aside Rule, so the Board's order was vacated and remanded for the knowledge and equity-and-good-conscience analysis.
We conclude that Ms. Boyd is without fault under the plain terms of OPM's guidelines. The administrative judge's contrary finding was based on an erroneous interpretation of the law.
1052: Entitlement to FERS annuity supplement; whether military service must be excluded from calculation of annuity supplement under 5 U.S.C. § 8421(b)(4)(C) and OPM regulation
As a result, Mr. Griswold's military service was properly excluded from the calculation of his annuity supplement.
1173: Entitlement to a CSRS retirement annuity: whether Mata served in a CSRS-covered position, so as to be eligible for an annuity or a deposit under 5 U.S.C. 8333 and 5 C.F.R. 831.112.
Although Mr. Mata proved that he had more than twenty years of service as an employee, he has failed to show that he served in a position covered by the CSRS.
1387: Entitlement to retirement annuity computation: whether two periods of service (DOL service with refunded contributions and VA temporary service with no deposits) could be credited without deposits.
there is no entitlement to recomputation regarding time for which no deposits exist.
1396: Entitlement to a FERS retirement annuity after Brown withdrew all retirement deductions through refunds; the Board affirmed OPM's denial of the annuity.
We agree with the government that the Board did not err in affirming OPM's denial of Brown's application for retirement.
1430: Whether OPM properly offset Anderson's FERS disability retirement annuity by his Social Security disability insurance benefits under 5 U.S.C. 8452(a)(2)(A); the court held the Special Provisions annuity is a disability retirement subject to offset.
Therefore, OPM was correct to offset Mr. Anderson's disability retirement annuity by his SSDI benefits.
1431: Denial of Anderson's request to waive recovery of the overpayment of disability annuity; the court found no abuse of discretion in denying the waiver.
We find no abuse of discretion in denying Mr. Anderson a waiver.
1534: Retirement/disability annuity: overpayment of FERS disability annuity owed because annuitant's earnings exceeded the 80% cap; waiver denied as annuitant was at fault.
Mr. Nelson accepted retirement benefit payments when he knew or should have known he was ineligible to receive such benefits.
1535: Entitlement to adjustment of the recovery schedule based on financial hardship; Board found annuitant failed to show hardship.
Mr. Nelson failed to provide sufficient evidence asserting he is entitled to further schedule adjustments.
1599: Entitlement to FERS disability annuity payments during the period his earnings exceeded the statutory threshold under 5 U.S.C. § 8455; no exception or waiver permitted.
This court has consistently held that section 8455 does not provide for exceptions or waivers in its application.
1624: Waiver of FERS overpayment recovery under 5 U.S.C. § 8346(b): court held recovery would be unconscionable because of OPM's lengthy delays, and reversed the Board's refusal to waive.
Considering the totality of the circumstances, we conclude that OPM's recovery of the $33,127.42 overpayment would be unconscionable.
1625: Relinquishment of a valuable right or change in position for the worse (equity and good conscience prong): court held the AJ's analysis was not supported by substantial evidence and was contrary to law.
The AJ's analysis on this issue is not supported by substantial evidence and is erroneous.
1626: Financial hardship prong of the equity and good conscience analysis: court found no error in the AJ's finding that Gordon failed to show financial hardship without an updated questionnaire.
we find no error in the AJ's consideration of this issue.
1697: Entitlement to a CSRS deferred retirement annuity: whether Dullas's excepted-service temporary and indefinite service was covered service, and whether 5 C.F.R. § 831.303(a) converted that service into covered service.
Although Mr. Dullas may have had more than five years of creditable service, § 831.303(a) did not convert creditable excluded positions into CSRA covered service.
1813: Annuity overpayment: OPM's calculation of the existence and amount of the overpayment of federal disability retirement annuity, affirmed as supported by substantial evidence.
We find these determinations to be supported by substantial evidence.
1814: Waiver of overpayment recovery under 5 U.S.C. 8470(b): denial of waiver for failure to show equity and good conscience (financial hardship, detrimental change of position, unconscionability), affirmed.
Lastly, Mr. Maye has not provided any evidence demonstrating unconscionability.
1836: Entitlement to a CSRS retirement annuity: whether the employee's service was covered service and whether pre-October 1, 1982 creditable service entitles him to an annuity under 5 C.F.R. 831.303(a) despite no covered service.
We conclude that the Board properly ruled that Mr. Dominico is not eligible for a CSRS annuity.
1884: Denial of waiver of FERS disability annuity overpayment (set-aside rule, fault, equity and good conscience); Board's adjustment of repayment schedule not disputed
Thus, the Board properly affirmed OPM's decision denying Ms. Warrender a waiver from recovery of the overpayment.
1992: Survivor annuity entitlement: whether the retiree made a timely signed-writing election of a survivor annuity for his remarried spouse under 5 U.S.C. § 8339(j)(5)(C)(i); Board finding that no election was made was supported by substantial evidence.
We conclude that substantial evidence supports the Board's determination that Mr. Rakowsky did not elect a survivor annuity in a signed writing, as required by statute.
1993: Annual notice to annuitant: whether OPM adequately sent the annual notices of the right to elect a survivor annuity and whether the annuitant rebutted the presumption of receipt; held notices adequate and rebuttal insufficient.
We agree with the administrative judge and the Board, therefore, that Ms. Rakowsky did not sustain her burden to show that the annuitant did not receive the annual notices.
2061: Entitlement to FERS annuity and survivor benefits: the court held Mr. Cieslinski did not qualify for annuity payments (lacking five years of civilian service and having received a refund of FERS contributions), and that the survivor deposit provision did not apply to a former employee.
he requested and received a refund of his FERS contributions, which nullifies any annuity rights he had.
2176: Entitlement to enhanced CBPO retirement credit (secondary CBPO position) under 5 U.S.C. 8412(d); validity of OPM regulations and whether FLETC instructor position was a secondary position
We therefore affirm the final decision.
2280: Entitlement to CSRS deferred retirement annuity; Garcia never served in a CSRS-covered position during the required period, so OPM's denial was upheld.
The Board found that Mr. Garcia never served in a position covered by the CSRS. That finding is in accordance with law; the decision is affirmed.
2563: Entitlement to a redetermination of retirement annuity rights upon reemployment and retirement, or termination of disability annuity under 5 U.S.C. 8455(a); court held Thomas entitled only to a supplemental annuity for her reemployment period.

Accordingly, we hold that the Board correctly determined that Thomas was not eligible for termination or a redetermination of her annuity, and that she was only eligible for a supplemental annuity covering her period of reemployment from 2005 to 2009, in addition to her prior annuity.
2823: Entitlement to redeposit refunded CSRS retirement deductions under 5 U.S.C. 8334(d)(1); whether Delarosa is an 'employee' under 5 C.F.R. 831.112(a) and retained annuity rights after receiving a refund, so he could redeposit.
Because Mr. Delarosa is not an employee eligible to redeposit retirement deductions, we affirm.
2896: Entitlement to survivor annuity for former spouse; whether OPM's annual notices adequately informed annuitant of need to renew pre-divorce survivor election
we find no error in the Board's conclusion that OPM's annual notices to Mr. Williams were not defective.
2973: Entitlement to disability retirement annuity; application for disability retirement held untimely under 5 U.S.C. § 8337(b) and waiver for mental incompetence not shown
the statute required the OPM to reject Ms. Johnson's application as untimely, and the MSPB properly affirmed the OPM's decision to do so.
3020: Denial of waiver of FERS annuity overpayment (without fault and against equity and good conscience); Board affirmed OPM's denial of waiver.
We agree with Ms. Bailey that the Board applied the correct legal framework, and we conclude substantial evidence supports the Board's findings.
3021: Denial of adjustment to the repayment schedule for the FERS overpayment; Board found no showing of financial hardship warranting a lower installment.

Contrary to Ms. Bailey's assertion on appeal, the Board considered her financial situation in determining whether OPM's adjusted repayment schedule of $50 per month would cause her financial hardship.
3139: Entitlement to survivor annuity benefits; whether the annuitant timely elected a survivor annuity under 5 U.S.C. § 8339(j)(5)(C) within two years of remarriage, and whether the late beneficiary designation showed intent to elect.
The Board found that Lewis failed to elect a survivor annuity for Williams within the two-year period prescribed by statute.
3585: Entitlement to survivor annuity under FERS/CSRS; whether retiree timely elected survivor annuity for remarried spouse within two-year statutory period
Because Mr. Taylor failed to timely elect Mrs. Taylor as his beneficiary, we affirm the Board's decision.
3764: Entitlement to a CSRS survivor annuity: whether the deceased spouse's first and second periods of federal service were covered service under the CSRA, so that the survivor annuity was payable.
We agree with the government that the AJ did not err in affirming OPM's denial of Ms. Yandoc's request for a survivor annuity.
3786: Entitlement to FERS annuity supplement under 5 U.S.C. § 8421(a)(1) for a disability retiree (§ 8451) who does not meet the age and service requirements of § 8412(d).
Thus, the plain text of §§ 8421(a)(1) and 8412(d) make clear that Mr. Pybas is not entitled to a FERS annuity supplement because he failed to satisfy the age and service requirements of § 8412(d).
3889: Entitlement to a CSRS retirement annuity after the annuitant received a refund of retirement contributions, which voids annuity rights under 5 U.S.C. § 8342(a); the court held she was not entitled to the annuity and that she could not redeposit because she is not a current employee.
Substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that Ms. Jenks failed to demonstrate she is entitled to an annuity.
3980: Entitlement to CSRS annuity: the court held service under a nonpermanent, indefinite appointment was not covered service, so the employee was not eligible for a CSRS annuity, and the reduced-annuity provision in 5 C.F.R. § 831.303(a) did not apply.
We agree with the government that the AJ did not err in affirming the denial of Cristobal's request for retirement benefits.
4102: Survivor annuity deposit under 5 U.S.C. 8418: the court held OPM's calculation of the required deposit for the survivor annuity was correct.
We reject, therefore, Hirschfield's claim that section 8418 abridges her constitutional equal protection guarantee.
4192: Calculation of disability retirement annuity; high-3 average salary properly included AUO premium pay, so OPM's recalculation was upheld.
Substantial evidence supports the MSPB's decision that OPM properly recalculated Mr. Lepore's retirement salary and annuities to include AUO.
4200: Entitlement to a CSRS retirement annuity: whether Villaruel's temporary, term, and indefinite excepted service was covered service under the CSRA, and whether 5 C.F.R. § 831.303(a) supplied coverage.

Because Mr. Villaruel failed to establish that he performed "covered service" during his employment, particularly during one of the last two years preceding his separation in 1992, and because § 831.303(a) is not a basis for coverage under the CSRA, Mr. Villaruel is not entitled to a CSRS retirement annuity.
4220: Entitlement to FERS retirement annuity credit: whether 87 days of Army National Guard service in 1977-1978 counts as creditable military service under 5 U.S.C. 8401(31) and 10 U.S.C. 12602, requiring a formal federal call-up.

We conclude that the Board did not err in holding that Mr. McGrath must show that, for the 87 days in dispute, he was formally ordered into federal service, pursuant to Title 10, by the President or other federal authority.
4346: Former spouse survivor annuity entitlement: whether the divorce terminated the survivor annuity election and whether a later election or court order restored Beckstead's entitlement.
The Board correctly concluded that Mrs. Beckstead failed to prove that she is entitled to a survivor annuity.
4478: Retirement annuity calculation: whether OPM properly excluded premium pay differential and relocation allowances from basic pay in computing the high-three average for Grover's annuity; the court held the exclusions consistent with the governing statutes and regulations.
Accordingly, the AJ affirmed OPM's decision relating to Mr. Grover's retirement annuity.
4685: Entitlement to CSRS deferred retirement annuity: whether Lledo's Navy service was covered service under 5 U.S.C. 8333 and whether 5 C.F.R. 831.303(a) converted creditable service into covered service, so as to entitle him to retirement benefits and a CSRDF deposit.

Because substantial evidence supports the Board's conclusion that Mr. Lledo's service was excluded from CSRDF coverage, the decision that Mr. Lledo is not entitled to CSRS benefits is in accordance with law.
5010: Termination of FERS disability annuity under 5 U.S.C. 8455(a)(2) after earning capacity was restored before age 60; OPM's interpretation of 5 C.F.R. 844.402 to count employer health-and-welfare payments received in cash as income was upheld as not plainly erroneous.
Ms. Green has not demonstrated—nor can we conclude—that treating these cash payments as income for purposes of determining earning capacity is plainly erroneous or inconsistent with the regulation.
5011: Denial of waiver of recovery of annuity overpayments and denial of adjustment to the repayment schedule; Board's findings upheld as supported by substantial evidence.
On review, Ms. Green has not demonstrated that the Board's waiver and adjustment decisions lacked substantial evidence or were otherwise arbitrary and capricious.
6035: Entitlement to survivor annuity: whether claimant was a 'widow' married for at least 9 months immediately before the employee's death under 5 U.S.C. § 8341(a)(1)

We conclude that the Gibsons' marriage did not last "9 months," a phrase whose "ordinary public meaning," Bostock v. Clayton County, 140 S. Ct. 1731, 1738 (2020), counts time using calendar months as the unit.
6624: Entitlement to FERS retirement annuity: whether West Point cadet time counts as civilian service under 5 U.S.C. § 8410 five-year eligibility threshold
We agree with the Board that Mr. Montelongo's cadet service was not "civilian service."
6625: Reliance on Air Force HR buy-back advice and OPM handbook to override statutory eligibility requirement; held not to override clear statutory language
In any event, neither OPM's handbook nor a government employee's advice overrides the clear language of the statute.
6696: Entitlement to civil service retirement annuity credit for Period One (June 21-30, 1982) of concurrent civilian and terminal-leave military service; the court held 8332(c)(2) does not bar civilian credit for that concurrent service.
We agree with Mr. Miller that the bar of § 8332(c)(2) does not apply to his claim with regard to Period One.
6697: Entitlement to civil service retirement annuity credit for Period Two (Aug. 27-Oct. 25, 1990); the court found substantial evidence did not support the Board's finding of leave-without-pay status, so the period is concurrent service and creditable.
we conclude that substantial evidence does not support the Board's finding that Mr. Miller was in leave-without-pay status during Period Two.
6698: Entitlement to civil service retirement annuity credit for Period Three (Aug. 22, 1994-Dec. 22, 1995), where military service was retroactively restored and civilian service voided, and no deposit or military pay waiver was made.

Because Mr. Miller is deemed to have had no civilian service during Period Three and because he has not made a deposit or waived his military retirement pay for this period, § 8332(c)(2) bars his claim for the period.
6720: Entitlement to a deferred annuity under 5 U.S.C. 8333(a)-(b): Labio's records show no service in a covered position, so he does not qualify; 5 C.F.R. 831.303(a) does not convert non-covered service into covered service.

Because Mr. Labio's petition for review depends on his unavailing § 831.303(a) argument, and because the record demonstrates that he otherwise fails to qualify for a deferred annuity, we affirm the Board's final decision and deny Mr. Labio's petition for review.
6897: Retirement annuity overpayment: whether OPM proved by preponderance of the evidence an overpayment of interim CSRS annuity payments, based on the refund of retirement deductions

Substantial evidence supports the MSPB's determination that the OPM demonstrated by a preponderance of the evidence that Ms. Dillard was "well-aware that she had applied for th[e] refund" and received it.
6907: Entitlement to CSRS deferred retirement annuity for 1957-1963 indefinite-appointment service; service was not covered service and 5 C.F.R. 831.303(a) does not create independent coverage.
Because § 831.303(a) is not an independent basis for coverage under the CSRA, the Board did not err in affirming OPM's determination that Mr. Eclarin is not entitled to an annuity.
7323: Entitlement to CSRS annuity; whether federal service was covered service under the CSRA so as to entitle the petitioner to an annuity
Thus, the AJ correctly determined that Reboja is not eligible for a CSRS annuity because his appointment was not covered service.
7644: Entitlement to immediate retirement annuity under 5 U.S.C. § 8336; court held Watkins was terminated by November 6, 2005, lacked creditable service and age requirements after that date, so OPM's denial was sustained.
Accordingly, Mr. Watkins has failed to show error in finding that he was terminated by November 6, 2005.
7755: Entitlement to a CSRS deferred annuity: Bagat was not eligible because his positions were indefinite or not-to-exceed appointments that were not covered positions, and his deposit and creditable-service arguments did not convert them to covered service. Board decision affirmed.
The Board's holding that Bagat is not eligible for a CSRA annuity is supported by substantial evidence and not contrary to law or arbitrary or capricious.
7889: Entitlement to a FERS deferred annuity: the Board's affirmance of OPM's denial, based on finding that Lemon applied for and received a refund of retirement deductions under 5 U.S.C. § 8424(a), so the annuity was void.
We therefore see no error in the AJ's decision affirming OPM's denial of Mr. Lemon's application for a deferred annuity.
8003: Entitlement to FERS survivor lump-sum death benefits: whether the substantial-compliance doctrine can excuse the unsigned 2017 beneficiary designation under 5 U.S.C. 8424(d); held the signature requirement is mandatory and benefits denied.
The substantial-compliance doctrine has no role here where it would conflict with § 8424(d)'s literal requirement that a designation be 'signed.'
8051: Entitlement to FERS disability retirement: the Board's finding that Courtney failed to show her disability made her unable to render useful and efficient service was affirmed.
we cannot set aside the Board's conclusion that Ms. Courtney failed to show that she was unable "to render useful and efficient service" in light of her disability.
8066: Entitlement to CSRS deferred retirement annuity: whether Senence's Navy service in the Philippines was covered service under the CSRA, given temporary/indefinite appointments, non-CSRS FEPI coverage, and no CSRS deductions withheld.
We find that the Board's decision was supported by substantial evidence.
8312: Entitlement to former spouse survivor annuity under FERS/CSRS: the court held the former spouse was not entitled to a survivor annuity because no pre-divorce election existed, the divorce decree did not expressly provide for one, and the applicant bears the burden of proving entitlement.
Because substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that Ms. Kimble-Davis did not establish she is entitled to the benefits, we affirm.
8383: Entitlement to primary law enforcement officer retirement credit (FERS LEO coverage) for June 2005 to November 2009. The Board applied the wrong analysis under Crowley: it failed to make two independent findings (position description alone, then actual duties alone), failed to separately assess vigorousness, and made contradictory hazardousness findings. The court vacated and remanded without deciding entitlement.

But our precedent is clear that the Board must make two independent findings: the first must be based on the position description evidence alone, and if that finding is adverse to the employee, the second must be based solely on evidence of his or her actual duties.
8652: Entitlement to CSRS retirement annuity: whether Apiag's service was covered service under the Civil Service Retirement Act, and whether 5 C.F.R. § 831.303(a) creates entitlement to an annuity for excluded service.
We hold that substantial evidence supports the Board's conclusion that Mr. Apiag never held a covered service position under the Act, and he is therefore ineligible for a CSRS annuity.
9067: Whether Globokar was properly assigned to FERS rather than CSRS under the FERS exclusion provisions; the Board's merits ruling that she was not entitled to CSRS coverage was affirmed.
Mere acceptance of an offer of employment to begin later does not constitute being employed in the position.
9226: Entitlement to former spouse survivor annuity; whether statutorily required notice was ineffective and decedent intended former spouse annuity
Because the Board's finding that OPM provided the statutorily mandated notice of annuity election rights is not supported by substantial evidence, we reverse.
9524: FERS annuity credit for non-deduction service: whether OPM properly denied credit absent payment of the required deposit, and whether installment payments or waiver of the deposit were permissible
she has identified no statute or regulation requiring the OPM to accept deposit payments in installments, even where the employee is suffering "financial hardship."
10712: Entitlement to FERS disability retirement: OPM's disallowance of an untimely disability retirement application was affirmed, so the annuity claim failed.
Because Ms. Webb has not shown that her application was filed within the statutory deadline or that waiver of the one-year time limit is warranted, we affirm the Board decision.
11420: Entitlement to FERS disability retirement: whether Coggins completed the 18 months of creditable service, based on the disputed start and last-day-of-pay dates in her IRR.
The Board affirmed the Office of Personnel Management's denial of her claim for disability retirement benefits. We affirm.
11552: Entitlement to FERS disability retirement benefits. The Board's finding that Nassar did not show medical inability to perform useful and efficient service was upheld as an unreviewable factual determination. The court found the Board erred in applying a five-year minimum service requirement, but held the error harmless.
we are precluded from reviewing the factual underpinnings of the Board's disability determination.
11694: Entitlement to FERS law enforcement officer retirement coverage; the claimant failed to carry the burden of showing compliance with the formal written request requirement
The Board’s ruling that Mr. LaCroix failed to carry his burden to prove that he complied with 5 C.F.R. § 842.804(c) is supported by substantial evidence.
11835: FERS disability annuity overpayment: the Board upheld OPM's calculation of the $61,531 overpayment arising from retroactive Social Security benefits, including the offset and the exclusion of health premium deductions.
The Board's findings regarding the amount of overpayment were supported by substantial evidence.
11836: Waiver of FERS overpayment under the equity and good conscience standard: the Board upheld OPM's no-waiver determination under the Set-Aside Rule because Casarez was on notice to set aside the SSA payment.
The Board's finding that Casarez was on notice of her repayment obligation and to set aside the Social Security payment in June 2018 was supported by substantial evidence.
11837: Adjustment of monthly repayment installments for financial hardship: the Board upheld OPM's refusal to lower the installment amount because Casarez did not submit financial information.
The Board's finding concerning Casarez's request for an adjusted monthly repayment amount is supported by substantial evidence.
11888: Entitlement to a FERS survivor annuity: Gloria Slagle was not eligible for a survivor annuity based on her spouse's federal service because he did not elect her as a post-retirement spouse within two years of marriage.
Gloria was not eligible because Wayne did not elect her as a post-retirement spouse within two years of their marriage.
11889: Payment of the FERS lump-sum survivor benefit to the designated beneficiary (former spouse Sarah) rather than to Gloria Slagle was proper.
Because Wayne did neither, under these circumstances, Sarah is entitled to the lump-sum benefit.
11900: Denial of waiver of FERS disability annuity overpayment under the equity and good conscience standard, applying the Set-Aside Rule and finding no exceptional circumstances; affirmed as supported by substantial evidence.
The Board's affirmance of the AJ's waiver finding under the Set-Aside Rule was supported by substantial evidence.
12049: Entitlement to annuity computation: whether the retiree received the full 1979 refund of retirement contributions, which OPM deducted from his annuity; the Board's finding that he failed to prove non-receipt was upheld.
We agree with the Board that Mr. White failed to carry his burden to prove non-receipt of the full amount of the authorized refund of $4,178.58 in 1979.
12050: Entitlement to annuity computation: whether OPM should have returned excess retirement deductions from service exceeding forty-one years and eleven months; the Board's finding that the claimant failed to prove entitlement was upheld.
We agree with the Board that Mr. White failed to carry his burden of proof.
12314: FERS disability retirement denial affirmed; Board's factual findings on disability not reviewable and no legal error found, so the denial of disability retirement stands.

To the extent Mr. Lee challenges the Board's weighing of the evidence, this challenge falls outside our limited scope of review in disability retirement appeals, which is substantially narrower than our review under the Administrative Procedure Act.
12336: Entitlement to CSRS annuity without offset: Bowden could not have been enrolled in CSRS without the offset because he lacked one-out-of-two years of covered service, so OPM was required to reduce his annuity under CSRS Offset.
Thus, as a matter of law, Mr. Bowden was not entitled to CSRS without offset and could not have elected it when he finally became eligible for retirement coverage in July 1987.
12509: Entitlement to CSRS deferred retirement annuity: the Board's finding that White applied for and received a 1991 refund, supported by substantial evidence, so she was not entitled to a deferred annuity.
We hold the Board's decision that Ms. White applied for and received a refund is supported by substantial evidence.
12595: Entitlement to FERS disability retirement; the court held that OPM's and the Board's factual findings on disability are not reviewable and affirmed denial of the application.
While we are sympathetic to Ms. Haynes, these constitute the "factual findings and conclusions on disability" that we are prohibited from reviewing.
12660: Entitlement to FERS retirement annuity: whether military service already compensated by military retired pay (disability-based) may be credited toward the FERS annuity under the double-crediting bar of 5 U.S.C. § 8411(c)(2); the court held it may not, and the Babakitis decision did not require otherwise.
The plain language of section 8411(c)(2) thus bars double crediting Mr. Stuart's military service in computing his FERS annuity.
12671: Entitlement to CSRS survivor annuity: whether the notarized April 1988 survivor-annuity waiver was valid against the claim that the signature was forged; MSPB found no forgery and the court found substantial evidence supported that finding.
We conclude that the MSPB's decision was supported by substantial evidence and thus affirm.
12672: Entitlement to CSRS survivor annuity: whether the waiver was invalid because Metz was mentally incompetent when she signed it in April 1988; MSPB found no proven incompetence and the court affirmed.
Those issues lead us to affirm the AJ's determination that Mrs. Metz did not meet her burden to show she was mentally incompetent when she signed the document in April 1988.
12734: Entitlement to a former spouse survivor annuity under 5 U.S.C. 8341(h)(1) and the divorce decree. The Board applied only the magic-words regulations and failed to apply the Fox/Downing three-part framework, which the court held was clear legal error requiring reversal and remand.
Instead of applying the Fox/Downing three-part framework, the Board seemingly engaged in a search for "magic words."
13000: FERS disability retirement eligibility: whether military service may be combined with civilian service to satisfy the 18-month civilian service requirement under 5 U.S.C. § 8451(a)(1)(A)
Military service therefore cannot count toward the required 18 months of civilian service.
13118: Entitlement to disability retirement: whether OPM overcame the Bruner presumption of disability by asserting a lack of objective medical evidence; court holds OPM cannot rely solely on lack of objective evidence and reverses, finding Garland entitled to disability retirement benefits.
we hold that OPM may not satisfy its burden of production under Bruner by simply asserting a lack of objective medical evidence.
13125: Existence and amount of FERS disability annuity overpayment (April 2016 to April 2019), decided on substantial evidence and gross-amount calculation; ruling for OPM
We conclude that substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that OPM has proven the existence and amount of the disputed overpayment by a preponderance of the evidence.
13126: Denial of waiver of repayment of the annuity overpayment under the set-aside rule and exceptional-circumstances standard; ruling for OPM
We similarly discern no error in the Board's determination that Ms. Nance was not entitled to a waiver of the obligation to repay overpayments received.
13152: FERS annuity overpayment: the funds erroneously deposited into petitioners' joint account were a recoverable debt under FERS regardless of the intended recipient.
the erroneously deposited funds constituted a debt under FERS regardless of whether the funds were intended for another annuitant.
13326: Entitlement to FERS deferred annuity: whether nearly eleven years of OWCP benefits after separation count as creditable service under 5 U.S.C. § 8411(d) toward the five-year minimum, including whether coerced resignation creates an exception.
Thus, we conclude that the Board did not abuse its discretion in affirming OPM's denial of Mr. Macura's request for a deferred annuity under the FERS.
13352: Entitlement to a CSRS survivor annuity for a post-retirement spouse. The court held Bell was ineligible because Mr. Bell did not elect with OPM a survivor annuity within two years of the marriage as 5 U.S.C. 8339(k)(2)(A) requires.

because Mr. Bell did not elect with OPM a CSRS survivor annuity within two years of his marriage to Ms. Bell (as 5 U.S.C. § 8339(k)(2)(A) requires) and no other route to such an annuity appears available on this record, we must affirm the Board's decision.
13364: Entitlement to FERS survivor annuity: whether claimant was married to the decedent at least nine months before death (widow status under 5 U.S.C. 8441(1)), resolved by finding no common law marriage in D.C. before the May 2020 civil ceremony.

Because we find no error in the Merit Systems Protection Board's determination that Mr. Schinella and Ms. Corcoran were married less than nine months before Mr. Schinella's passing, we affirm the denial of Ms. Corcoran's claim for survivor annuity benefits.
13406: Entitlement to FERS disability retirement: the Board's affirmance of OPM's denial, finding insufficient evidence that her medical conditions were incompatible with useful and efficient service; court declined to review the factual underpinnings.

we lack jurisdiction over the factual findings she challenges and do not perceive any "substantial departure from important procedural rights, a misconstruction of the governing legislation, or some like error 'going to the heart of the administrative determination'" in the Board's decision.
13422: Entitlement to a CSRS deferred retirement annuity: whether the petitioner proved service in a covered position under 5 U.S.C. 8333, given no evidence of CSRS deductions and no corroborating records.
Thus, the Board did not err in concluding that Mr. Duong had failed to prove his eligibility for an annuity under the statute.
13517: Whether Simpkins's refunded FERS contributions remain uncreditable and whether he was eligible to redeposit them, based on his resignation date and the settlement agreement.

Accordingly, the Board reasonably found that the execution date did not change the effective date of his resignation because the Settlement Agreement specifically required that he resign no later than April 16, 2009.
13522: Whether the Board erred by not considering his military service deposit for a CSRS calculation; court found no error since the FERS calculation included it.
we see no error in the Board's failure to consider it for a CSRS calculation, a calculation that Mr. Simpkins does not seek in this appeal.
13530: Entitlement to FERS disability retirement annuity; Board affirmed OPM denial finding no disabling condition; Federal Circuit lacks jurisdiction to review factual disability findings
we agree with OPM that we lack jurisdiction to review either OPM's disability-related factual findings or the Board's affirmance of OPM's findings.
13594: Whether OPM may apportion a retiree's FERS annuity supplement to a former spouse under 5 U.S.C. 8421(c) and 8467(a) absent express provision in the court order; court held OPM may apportion the supplement only when expressly provided for in a court order, affirming the Board for the annuitant.
we conclude that OPM cannot divide a retiree’s annuity supplement unless the division of the supplement is expressly provided for in a court order.
13967: Entitlement to CSRS retirement annuity and to make a non-covered service deposit under 5 U.S.C. § 8334(c); Caneda had no covered service, so he was not entitled to CSRS benefits.
because covered service is a statutory prerequisite to both an annuity and any deposit under § 8334(c), he is not entitled to benefits under the CSRS as a matter of law.
13995: Entitlement to FERS disability retirement: whether the Board properly refused to consider the employee's inability to commute in deciding whether she could render useful and efficient service under 5 U.S.C. § 8451(a)(1)(B).
Accordingly, the Board correctly refused to consider Chafin's inability to commute in concluding that she was not unable to render useful and efficient service.
14008: Entitlement to a survivor annuity as an incapable-of-self-support child; Board found no showing of disability incurred before age 18 under 5 U.S.C. § 8341, so the annuity was denied.

substantial evidence supports the Board's determination that Ms. Williams did not demonstrate that she was diagnosed with a disability before age 18 that would render her eligible for a survivor annuity under 5 U.S.C. § 8341.
14032: Alternative merits holding on computation of Brown's CSRS retirement annuity: excess contribution crediting under 5 U.S.C. 8342(h) and the annuity reduction under 5 C.F.R. 831.303(a) were proper, so the board's affirmance of OPM's calculation was not shown to be erroneous.
we note, moreover, that even if Brown's petition for review had been timely filed, she fails to show error in the board's decision affirming OPM's calculation of her CSRS annuity.
14524: Survivor annuity computation for a retiree with combined CSRS and FERS service: whether the survivor annuity is 50% of the retiree's annuity under FERS (§ 8442(a)) or computed under the compound CSRS/FERS formula.

FERSA, which undisputedly governs, requires computing Ms. Sullivan's survivor annuity at 50% of Mr. Sullivan's retirement annuity. As this is the calculation OPM made and the Board affirmed, we affirm.
14541: FERS disability annuity overpayment: affirmed OPM's calculation of a net overpayment of $11,036.76 and rejected the argument that the Treasury Offset Program or SSA had already collected the debt.
Substantial evidence supports the Board's decision affirming OPM's calculation of a net overpayment of $11,036.76.
14704: Entitlement to FERS annuity supplement after probationary termination; annuitant not entitled because annuity was not received under the enumerated provisions of 5 U.S.C. 8421(a)(1) or (a)(2).

Because Ms. Dixon-Johnson does not receive her annuity under any of the provisions listed in § 8421(a)(1) or (2), the Board did not err in affirming OPM's denial of Ms. Dixon-Johnson's request for an annuity supplement.
14705: Calculation of high-three average salary for FERS annuity; OPM's weighting of salary rates by period in effect under 5 U.S.C. 8401(3) upheld.

Section 8401(3) explicitly states that each rate must be "weighted by the period it was in effect." The Board therefore did not err in affirming OPM's calculation of Ms. Dixon-Johnson's high-three salary.
14878: Entitlement to FERS disability retirement annuity; the Board affirmed OPM's denial of Hautala's application for disability retirement.
For the reasons explained below, we affirm.
14959: Entitlement to a former spouse survivor annuity under 5 U.S.C. § 8341(h); the divorce decree and marital settlement agreement did not expressly provide for a survivor annuity, so OPM's denial was upheld.

Thus, even though the Divorce Decree and the MSA provided Ms. Valdez with a portion of Mr. Abeita's retirement benefits during Mr. Abeita's lifetime, the Divorce Decree and the MSA do not expressly provide for an award of survivor annuity benefits to Ms. Valdez upon Mr. Abeita's death.
15018: Entitlement to FERS disability retirement; the Board's denial was affirmed because substantial evidence supported the finding that the applicant was not disabled while employed, and OPM's physical disability factual findings are not reviewable.
Thus, "we must reject challenges to the Board's factual determinations on physical disability."
15046: Whether the neck and back conditions were part of the FERS disability retirement claim, given they were not listed in the applicant's statement of disability.
We see no error in the Board’s determination.
15170: Denial of waiver of repayment of a FERS disability annuity overpayment under OPM's set-aside rule and the exceptional-circumstances standard; Board found no exceptional circumstances and financial hardship insufficient.
We discern no error in the Board's determination that Ms. Gavin was not entitled to a waiver of the obligation to repay the overpayment.
